purpose: Instructions for AI agents (and humans) on how to add a new artwork to the portfolio at portofolio.html. Follow these steps exactly so new entries match the existing ones.
when_user_says: The user drops a new image into images/portofolio/display/ (often a PNG with a UUID-style name, untracked in git) and gives a title, medium/year and dimensions.

inputs_needed.title: Display title exactly as the user writes it, e.g. 'D. Dotl'
inputs_needed.size_cm: height × width in cm, e.g. '109 × 69 cm' (use the × character, as the user gives it, height first)
inputs_needed.if_missing: Ask the user for any missing field. Do not invent title, medium or dimensions.

steps.name: Look at the image
steps.detail: Read the image file to write accurate alt text.

steps.name: Pick a filename
steps.detail: Lowercase, spaces and dots become underscores, only a-z 0-9 _ - allowed, .jpg extension. 'D. Dotl' -> d_dotl.jpg. Use the same filename in display/ and thumbs/.

steps.name: Create the display and thumbnail JPGs
steps.detail: Display: full image as JPEG, quality 85, max 1500px on the long side (~200-700 KB). Thumb: max 600px on the long side, JPEG quality 80 (~100-140 KB). Convert PNG to JPG. Then delete the original UUID-named PNG from display/.
commands: sips -s format jpeg -s formatOptions 85 display/<SOURCE>.PNG --out display/<name>.jpg
sips -s format jpeg -s formatOptions 80 -Z 600 display/<SOURCE>.PNG --out thumbs/<name>.jpg
steps.alternative: generate_thumbnails.py does the same with Pillow, but it reads from images/portofolio/originals/ (which currently does not exist) and caps display at 1500px.

steps.name: Do not commit .DS_Store files
steps.detail: Ignore .DS_Store changes in git status. Never stage them.

steps.name: Add the HTML entry to the right material section
steps.detail: portofolio.html is split into <section class="works" id="..."> blocks by MATERIAL: #dotl, titled 'DOTL' (EVERYTHING on fabric, acrylic on fabric or plain 'Fabric', whatever the title), #cotton (compressed cotton), #wood-metal (wood, metal), #paper (pen on paper, always LAST). Insert the new <li> as the FIRST child of that section's <ul class="works__grid"> (newest first), then bump the 'N works' counter in that section's header. Nothing else needs updating: the lightbox order, prev/next, 'x / N' counter, deep-link URL (#<id>) and schema.org VisualArtwork data are all built from the entries at runtime.
notes: Indentation: 24 spaces for <li>, matching the existing entries.
slug = title lowercased, every run of non a-z0-9 characters replaced by '-', trimmed. 'D. Dotl' -> d-dotl. Must be unique on the page; it is the shareable link (portofolio.html#d-dotl).

thumb_w / thumb_h = the REAL pixel size of the thumbnail (check with: sips -g pixelWidth -g pixelHeight <file>). The masonry grid uses them to reserve the right space. Do not set 600x600 for non-square images.
alt text: one sentence describing the artwork visually (form, colors, material), ending with a period.
Caption format: medium line like 'Acrylic on fabric, 2026' (must contain the 4-digit year, it feeds the structured data); size line like '109 × 69 cm' (height × width, with the × character).

A material that has no section yet (e.g. ceramics): add a new <section class="works" id="ceramics"> before the paper section with the same header markup, plus a link <a href="#ceramics"> in <nav class="sections-nav">.

steps.name: Verify
steps.detail: Confirm both JPGs exist, the paths in the HTML match, and git status shows only the new files plus portofolio.html (apart from .DS_Store).

steps.name: Commit only if asked
steps.detail: Do not commit or push unless the user asks. Previous commit style: 'Add <title> to portfolio' with a one-line body.

file_locations.sections: Pieces are grouped by material in portofolio.html: dotl (all fabric works), cotton, wood-metal, paper (last).

user_preferences.ordering: Grouped by material; within a section newest first. 'Pen on paper' stays as the last, separate section.
user_preferences.format: JPG for both display and thumbnail, descriptive snake_case filenames.
user_preferences.look: White gallery-wall background (#fefefe, matches the near-white padding baked into the JPGs), serif titles, violet accent. Do not switch to a dark or cream background without asking: the images have white margins.
user_preferences.sharing: Page has Open Graph/Twitter tags pointing at images/portofolio/display/d_dotl.jpg; if the user asks for a different cover image, change og:image, og:image:alt and twitter:image in the <head>.
